title: Inheritance check
instructions: Five questions on inheritance and special methods.

options: The base class that Dog builds on
questions.explanation: The class in parentheses is the base class. Dog inherits its methods and can override them.

questions.prompt: Dog does not define __init__, but Animal does. What happens when you write Dog('Rex')?
questions.explanation: A subclass inherits everything it does not override, including __init__.

questions.prompt: What does super().__init__(name) do inside a subclass?
questions.explanation: super() reaches the base class, so you can reuse its setup and then add more.

questions.prompt: Which special method controls what print(obj) shows?
questions.explanation: print uses __str__. Without it you get an unhelpful default like <__main__.Dog object at 0x...>.

questions.prompt: A Car has an Engine. Which design fits best?
options: Car stores an Engine object as an attribute
questions.explanation: Inheritance means is-a. A car has an engine, so store the engine as an attribute.

title: Dog and Cat
instructions:
The base class `Animal` is already written. Write two subclasses:

- `Dog`: `speak()` returns `"Woof"`.
- `Cat`: `speak()` returns `"Meow"`.

Do not copy `__init__` or `__str__`. Then print `Dog("Rex")` and, on the next line, `Cat("Tom")`:

```text
Rex says Woof
Tom says Meow
```

tests.expected_stdout:
Rex says Woof
Tom says Meow
